title: Learning from Human Preferences
mechanism_summary: Optimize a policy from pairwise human preferences over trajectories rather than hand-written reward functions.
limits: Preference labels are expensive and encode the evaluator's observable proxy; the method does not solve distribution shift or evaluator error.

title: AI Safety via Debate
mechanism_summary: Two agents argue for competing answers while a judge evaluates the debate, making difficult claims recursively inspectable.
limits: The judge can be manipulated, debate quality depends on the question decomposition, and empirical demonstrations were narrow.

title: Learning to Summarize from Human Feedback
mechanism_summary: Train a reward model from human comparisons of summaries, then optimize a language model against that learned preference signal.
limits: Optimization can exploit reward-model blind spots; summaries are short and the task does not establish robust generalization to open-ended claims.

title: Learning to Reason with Human Feedback
mechanism_summary: Instruction-following models are fine-tuned from demonstrations and ranked outputs, then optimized with reinforcement learning from human feedback.
limits: The objective is a proxy for helpfulness; preference optimization can reward style or agreement, and the training distribution remains bounded.

title: Improving Mathematical Reasoning with Process Supervision
mechanism_summary: Reward each intermediate reasoning step with a process reward model instead of scoring only the final answer.
limits: Step labels are costly, correctness of a local step can depend on later context, and process supervision was evaluated primarily on mathematical reasoning.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report
mechanism_summary: Scale a multimodal transformer with post-training and alignment procedures to improve broad language, coding, and reasoning performance.
limits: The report withholds most architecture and training details, and benchmark performance does not imply reliable autonomous research or factuality.

title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization
mechanism_summary: Use weak-model labels to fine-tune a stronger pretrained model, with confidence losses and bootstrapping to recover latent capability.
limits: Naive supervision does not recover the full strong model and fails on some preference data; the analogy to superhuman alignment is incomplete.

title: Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders
mechanism_summary: Use k-sparse autoencoders to decompose model activations into sparse features, controlling sparsity directly and evaluating reconstruction, probes, and downstream effects.
limits: Reconstruction and sparsity can improve while features remain unhelpful; sparse latent identities are not automatically causal or semantically correct.

title: Prover-Verifier Games Improve Legibility of Language Model Outputs
mechanism_summary: Alternate training a verifier and a helpful or adversarial prover so correct solutions become easier for weaker evaluators to check.
limits: Early adversarial proofs can fool the verifier; the method was tested on grade-school mathematics and legibility is not equivalent to truth.

title: MLE-bench
mechanism_summary: Evaluate agents on 75 Kaggle machine-learning competitions with compute, data, and engineering tools, scoring bronze-level success and resource scaling.
limits: Tasks can be contaminated by pretraining and leaderboard feedback; the environment is expensive and competition scores are not research novelty measures.

title: PaperBench
mechanism_summary: Benchmark agents reproducing 20 ICML papers using hierarchical, author-developed rubrics and an auxiliary judge-evaluation benchmark.
limits: Replication is different from discovering new science; LLM judges can disagree with experts, and the benchmark covers a small paper sample.

title: Weight-Sparse Transformers Have Interpretable Circuits
mechanism_summary: Train transformers with mostly zero weights, then prune task-specific circuits whose neurons and residual channels can be inspected directly.
limits: Sparsity trades capability for interpretability, and scaling beyond tens of millions of nonzero parameters remains unresolved.

title: Debugging Misaligned Completions with Sparse-Autoencoder Latent Attribution
mechanism_summary: Model-diffing selects SAE latents changed by problematic fine-tuning; activation steering and judged completions test whether those latents causally influence behavior.
limits: Latent selection and LLM grading are proxies; steering one latent may create off-target behavior and does not establish a complete causal model.

title: Deep Research System Card
mechanism_summary: A browsing agent decomposes research tasks, searches and pivots across web sources, reads files, and executes analysis code under a safety evaluation process.
limits: Browsing exposes prompt-injection, privacy, and source-quality risks; autonomous tool use remains bounded by evaluation tasks and human deployment controls.

title: Using Thousands of AI Agents to Uncover New Leads in Biological Data
mechanism_summary: Thousands of parallel agents analyze perturbation data and literature to connect gene disruptions with disease-related cell states and propose biological leads.
limits: The reported leads are hypotheses from existing data, not validated treatments; parallel agreement does not replace wet-lab replication or causal intervention.
